form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Paul (for himself, Mr. King, Mr. Crapo, and Mr. Lee) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary

form.official-title: To restore the integrity of the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution of the United States, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Fifth Amendment Integrity Restoration Act of 2019 or the FAIR Act.
Section 983 of title 18, United States Code, is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (b)(2)(A)—

subparagraph.text: by striking , and the property subject to forfeiture is real property that is being used by the person as a primary residence,; and
by striking , at the request of the person, shall insure and inserting shall ensure;

paragraph.text: in subsection (c)—

subparagraph.text: in paragraph (1), by striking a preponderance of the evidence and inserting clear and convincing evidence;
in paragraph (2), by striking a preponderance of the evidence and inserting clear and convincing evidence; and
by striking paragraph (3) and inserting the following:

paragraph.text: if the Government's theory of forfeiture is that the property was used to commit or facilitate the commission of a criminal offense, or was involved in the commission of a criminal offense, the Government shall establish, by clear and convincing evidence, that—

subparagraph.text: there was a substantial connection between the property and the offense; and
the owner of any interest in the seized property—

clause.text: used the property with intent to facilitate the offense; or
knowingly consented or was willfully blind to the use of the property by another in connection with the offense.

paragraph.text: in subsection (d)(2)(A), by striking an owner who and all that follows through upon learning and inserting an owner who, upon learning;

in subsection (f)(6), in the matter preceding paragraph (7), by inserting , and shall award to the claimant an amount equal to 3 times the value of the property seized and a reasonable attorney's fee before the period at the end; and
in subsection (i)—

subparagraph.text: by striking subparagraphs (A) and (B); and
by redesignating subparagraphs (C) through (E) as subparagraphs (A) through (C), respectively.

subsection.header: Probable cause hearing in connection with property seizures relating to certain monetary instruments transactions

paragraph.text: Section 5317 of title 31, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

subsection.header: Probable cause hearing in connection with property seizures relating to certain monetary instruments transactions

paragraph.text: Not later than 14 days after the date on which notice is provided under paragraph (2)—

subparagraph.text: a court of competent jurisdiction shall conduct a hearing on any property seized or restrained under subsection (c)(2) with respect to an alleged violation of section 5324; and
any property described in subparagraph (A) shall be returned unless the court finds that there is probable cause to believe that there is a violation of section 5324 involving the property.

paragraph.text: Each person from whom property is seized or restrained under subsection (c)(2) with respect to an alleged violation of section 5324 shall be notified of the right of the person to a hearing under paragraph (1).
The amendment made by paragraph (1) shall apply to property seized or restrained after the date of enactment of this Act.

section.text: Section 983(g)(2) of title 18, United States Code, is amended to read as follows:

paragraph.text: In making this determination, the court shall consider such factors as—

subparagraph.text: the seriousness of the offense;
the extent of the nexus of the property to the offense;
the range of sentences available for the offense giving rise to forfeiture;
the fair market value of the property; and
the hardship to the property owner and dependents.

section.text: Section 524(c)(6)(i) of title 28, United States Code, is amended by inserting from each type of forfeiture, and specifically identifying which funds were obtained from including criminal forfeitures and which were obtained from civil forfeitures, after deposits.

subparagraph.text: Any proceeding described in subparagraph (A) shall be commenced within 6 months of the entry of the order granting the motion.
by striking paragraph (5);

paragraph.text: in subsection (f)(1), in the matter preceding subparagraph (A), by striking (a) and inserting (a)(3)(A);
in subsection (g)(1), by striking (a)(4) and inserting (a)(3); and
by adding at the end the following:
Notwithstanding any other provision of law—

subparagraph.text: no Federal seizing agency may conduct nonjudicial forfeitures;
no property may be subject to forfeiture except through judicial process; and
no order of forfeiture may be entered except by a United States district court.

paragraph.text: In this subsection, the term nonjudicial forfeiture means an in rem action that permits the Federal seizing agency to start a forfeiture without judicial involvement.

section.text: The amendments made by this Act shall apply to—

paragraph.text: any civil forfeiture proceeding pending on or filed on or after the date of enactment of this Act; and
any amounts received from the forfeiture of property on or after the date of enactment of this Act.
